correctness.rationale: Every finite-colength ideal in k[[x,y]]/(y^2-x^(2d+1)) has a rank-two DVR-lattice Hermite form generated over k[[x]] by x^(b+h) and x^b(y+g(x)), with colength 2b+h. Closure under y is exactly x^h dividing x^(2d+1)-g^2. Odd valuation forces h<=2d+1; for each h the reduced parameter set has g coefficients only in degrees ceil(h/2)..h-1, an affine space A^(floor(h/2)) over any field including characteristic two. Contact with x is 0 only at colength zero, 1 for b=0,h>0, 2 for b>=1. Summation proves G=1+z(F-1)+z^2 Q^2 F/(1-Q^2); the fat-branch formula is correctly imported from the actual HJO Corollary 6.8 including denominator (Qz;QL)_u. Independent congruence enumeration over F2/F3 with d=2,3,h<=6 confirmed the reduced-scheme coefficient conditions; finite tests do not prove the all-field motivic claim.

It does not supply the new higher-odd-cusp input. Sōma--Watari 2015 fully classifies the same A_{2d} punctual ideals and affine cells over algebraically closed characteristic zero, so much geometry is prior and contact bookkeeping might be derivable implicitly. The unrefined 2025 cusp series matches z=1 but does not fix x-contact. The explicit all-field bivariate formula is best-of-knowledge not previously stated; PASS with serious implicit-derivability and unread 2025 full-text risks.

value.rationale: The cited 2026 primary source expressly motivates computing the exact contact input for unibranch singularities. The all-colength, all-higher-A_{2d}, all-field two-variable motivic series and its precise contact strata are a natural complete invariant not determined by an unrefined zeta alone; combining it with an attributed general theorem yields every fat-line addition. This is more than a normalized textbook computation even though the underlying ideal structure has prior descriptions.
